learning_outcomes.text: To have systematic knowledge and understanding of the key concepts and aspects of materials science and engineering.
To have adequate knowledge of materials science and engineering, including some knowledge at the forefront of its field in mechanical engineering.
To be aware of the multidisciplinary context of engineering.
To be able to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate, and solve problems in materials science and engineering using established methods.
To be able to design and conduct experiments in materials science and engineering, interpret data, and draw conclusions.
To have technical and laboratory competencies in materials science and engineering.

To demonstrate awareness of the responsibility of engineering practice, its social and environmental impact, and commitment to professional ethics, responsibility, and standards of engineering practice.
A systematic understanding of the key concepts and aspects of their branch of engineering.
Adequate knowledge of their branch of engineering, including some knowledge at the forefront of their field.
Awareness of the multidisciplinary context of engineering.
The ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate, and solve engineering problems using established methods.
Understanding of different methods and the ability to use them.
The ability to design and conduct experiments, interpret data, and draw conclusions.
Technical and laboratory competencies.

To demonstrate awareness of the responsibility of engineering practice, its social and environmental impact, and commitment to professional ethics, responsibility, and standards of engineering practice.

That students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is usually found at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that imply knowledge originating from the forefront of their field of study.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competencies typically demonstrated through the development and defense of arguments and problem-solving within their field of study.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, abilities, and skills in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge and ability to analyze and assess the social and environmental impact of technical solutions, and to apply environmental and sustainability technologies.
Ability to design and conduct experiments and to analyze and interpret the data obtained.
Knowledge of the fundamentals of materials science, technology, and chemistry. Understand the relationship between microstructure, synthesis or processing, and material properties.

syllabus_topics: Environmental impact of materials. Material life cycle. Population and materials. Reuse and recycling: circular economy. Industrial and urban solid waste. Separation and selection of MSW. Complex waste: transport vehicles.

Recycling of metals and alloys. Integral cycle of metals. Secondary metallurgy. Regeneration and welding of railway tracks. Pyrometallurgy: Steel scrap treatment. Aluminum recycling. Tinplate recycling. Hydrometallurgy: Recycling of heavy metals. Lead battery recycling. Battery recycling (general). Mercury management.

Recycling of ceramic materials. Separation and preparation of construction materials. Difference between glass and crystal. Color separation. Glass recycling. Manufacturing of containers, fibers, microspheres. Recycling of photovoltaic cells. Light bulbs, fluorescent tubes, and mercury lamps. Battery recycling: primary, Ni-Cd/Pb/Li-ion batteries.

Recycling of plastics and composites. Plastic separation treatment. Reuse of thermoplastics. Recycling of thermosets. "Bio" plastics. Separation of composite material elements. Recycling of GFRP and CFRP. Reuse or recycling: the cases of tires and Tetrapak.

Obtaining enriched uranium. Low-activity waste. High-activity waste: Centralized Temporary Storage (ATC) and Deep Geological Repository. Dismantling of a power plant. Recycling of nuclear fuel. Map of the future of nuclear energy.
assessment_rules: The general grading scheme is a Final Exam (40%) and Continuous Assessment (60%). Continuous Assessment includes Moodle questionnaires, short presentations, active participation in debates, and a final term paper/report with presentation, where the term paper's weight is double that of other continuous assessment components. Students with over 85% class attendance and active participation may pass solely based on their continuous assessment average, without a final exam. For the ordinary call, if continuous assessment is not fully completed, the final exam will account for 60% of the grade. For the extraordinary call, the final exam will account for 100% of the final grade.
